summary: Comprehensive backend (pytest 30 tests) + frontend (Playwright) testing of FIFA WC 2026 Predictor MVP. 100% backend pass rate. Frontend pages load, auth flow works, protected routes redirect, admin console functional, predictions UI uses click-to-expand pattern, awards form complete, View Squad links point to correct FIFA PDF URL. Scoring math verified end-to-end (2-1 -> +5, 1-0 -> +3, 0-2 -> 0; awards 4 correct -> +8). Note: server clock is at 2026-06-11 04:20 UTC so match #2 (kickoff 00:00 UTC) is correctly LOCKED; match #1 (15:00 UTC) is still open.

issues: Each match card requires clicking a 'PREDICT' button to reveal score-home-{n}/score-away-{n}/motm-{n}/save-pred-{n} inputs - this is by design but the data-testid documentation should mention this. Locked matches (kickoff passed) correctly hide the PREDICT button and show LOCKED badge.
result-home/result-away/result-motm/result-submit selectors only render after clicking an admin-pick-{n} row in the match list. This is by design (expand-on-select pattern).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 558 lines - approaching the 700-line guideline limit. Consider splitting routes into modules (auth_router, matches_router, admin_router) before adding more features.

In admin_set_result (server.py:400-413), recomputing total_points inside the per-prediction loop runs N aggregation queries for the same user when multiple predictions exist for the same user on the same match (currently impossible due to unique index, so functionally fine). Minor inefficiency only.
matches_seed.json contains 'time' as a naive datetime string ('2026-06-11 15:00:00'). The code defensively re-stamps tz to UTC, but ISO-8601 with 'Z' suffix would be cleaner and self-documenting.
/api/auth/forgot-password returns the reset_token directly in the JSON response (server.py:207). This is fine for demo/MVP but must be removed before production (token should only be emailed).

Awards lock uses 'first match by match_no' (server.py:295). If FIFA reschedules and an earlier kickoff time gets assigned a higher match_no, the lock would be incorrect. Recommend ordering by 'time' instead.
CORS uses allow_origin_regex='.*' with allow_credentials=True (server.py:466). Works for preview but should be tightened to an explicit allowlist for production.
test_credentials: Admin: admin@worldcup.com / Admin@2026 ; new users created via /api/auth/register with TEST_ email prefix
seed_data_creation: Tests create disposable users with TEST_ email prefix; scoring tests use match #50; awards scoring test creates an isolated user.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Server clock is in June 2026 (during the tournament). Match #1 kickoff 2026-06-11 15:00 UTC, Match #2 already locked at 00:00 UTC. Use match numbers >= 50 for prediction tests to ensure they remain unlocked. After admin/matches/{n}/result is called, that match's predictions become 'scored=true' and user total_points equals (sum of scored prediction points) + award points. Award winners scoring overwrites user.total_points to (match_total + award_pts) per user; this is correct given the seeded data but be aware if you add new users between calls.
rca of the issue: No real bugs found. Two initial test failures (test_register_sets_cookie email casing and test_update_prediction_upsert on match #2) were test bugs - email is correctly lowercased by API and match #2 is correctly locked by the kickoff time. Tests were updated to use email.lower() comparison and future match numbers (80, 81) for prediction tests, plus a new test_prediction_locked_for_started_match positive test verifying the lock behavior.
